items.title: Centre Wellington Hydro Annual General Meeting
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Wayne Dyce, President, Centre Wellington Hydro gave a presentation reviewing the company structure, Centre Wellington Hydro performance & rates, capital project investment, customer engagement, and a review of the financials.
Councillor Craddock arrived at 1:04pm
W. Dyce reviewed the requirements of the Annual General Meeting and indicated there is an additional request this year to permit borrowing for capital investment.
He further highlighted the systems reliability and efficiency and updated Council on planned upgrades including plans for a new station and customer engagement completed this past year.
W. Dyce responded to questions regarding the Milligan Park location for the station, low income assistance program, employee benefits and streetlight maintenance.

items.title: Mayor's County Council Report
notes: Mayor Watters updated Council regarding the Grand River Conservation Authority completion of the repairs to the low-level bridge at the Elora Gorge Conservation Area. He further indicated the County of Wellington is looking at a photo enforcement agreement to implement traffic control with automated cameras, investing costs for possible upgrades to the Elora and Rothsay waste facilities and reported the increase in waste bag fees for 2024, the first increase since 2016.

Decision Report OP02/23 and RZ05/23: 19-19A East Mill St.
Report from M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services

Mariana Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services outlined the report indicating the property is a 0.3 hectare site, on the east side of Geddes St, south of East Mill Street in the Elora Salem Urban Centre. It currently contains a vacant residential dwelling along East Mill Street and a shed proposed to be demolished, as well as a former industrial use heritage building, which housed the Elora Concrete Burial Vault factory. The property is in an area designated “Residential” in the Official Plan and adjacent to the “Central Business District Commercial” designation to the west and north, with Residential to the east.

She indicated the owner is seeking an Official Plan and zoning amendment to change it from Residential - R1A to Central Business District and C1 – commercial exception zoning. The purpose of the applications are to facilitate an infill development of 18 residential units and ground floor commercial space in a proposed 4 storey mixed use building, with a commercial building at the rear of the property closest to the river that will house a future restaurant. Staff anticipate a future application for a plan of condominium on the property.

motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receive report COR2024-27 dated June 10, 2024 as information. AND THAT the following direction be provided to staff in the preparation of the 2025 Draft Budget: 1: Maintain a 2025 tax rate increase equal to or less than 4.5% excluding asset and termite management allocations, 2: That staff instate an increase equivalent to a 2% increase in taxation during the 2025 Draft Budget process to generate the required funds to mitigate the funding gap within specific asset types identified in the Township's 2022 Asset Management Plan. 3: That staff instate an increase of $88,500 to the total levy requirement for the 2025 Draft Budget process to generate the funds required to ensure sufficient Termite Management program funding. 4: Assume 2025 assessment growth equal to 2.5%, to be used to fund budget increases considered to be growth in nature, with assessment growth figures to be updated in November, when received. 5: Increase fees and charges for 2025 by 4.5%, other than where pressure on rates indicates an alternate rate change. 6: Maintain a 3-year funding average of approximately $1,900,000 in growth related capital projects to be funded by development charges within the Draft Ten Year Capital Forecast. 7: Allocate the following funding to the Draft Capital Budget: · $7,870,000 in combined General Capital Reserve, Canada Community-Building Fund (CCBF), OLG Funds, and Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund (OCIF). · An increase in funding to the tax supported Equipment, Vehicle, and Facility Replacement Reserves to support budgetary needs. 8: That Council approve the proposed 2025 Budget Schedule.
